projects.name: Build technical capacities of value chain actors for efficient and inclusive sunflower, maize, beans, and fishery value chains in Tanzania (AFDP)
projects.description:
Support to strengthen sunflower, maize, beans, and fishery value chain in Tanzania. i) designed to enhance market access, value addition, and private sector development for smallholder farmers. Its core strategy revolves around improving the seed business and fish market systems, with a strong emphasis on sustainable agricultural practices and inclusive growth. The programme aims to increase the use of quality seeds by supporting a sustainable supply of locally adapted and climate-resilient varieties. This effort targets 25% of local farming activities, enabling farmers to replace open-pollinated varieties every three years while building their capacity to maintain seed quality. To achieve its goals, AFDP focuses on four strategic areas. First, it establishes regional multi-stakeholder innovation platforms that bring together public, private, and associative actors. These platforms coordinate seed demand and supply, promote climate-smart agriculture, and support the development of professional seed producer and distributor organizations. They also facilitate annual stakeholder meetings and use digital tools for planning and monitoring seed-related activities. Second, the programme strengthens the supply and accessibility of improved seeds by developing agro-dealer networks and village input shops, particularly those managed by women and youth. It promotes partnerships between local agro-dealers and national seed producers, supports group purchases of seeds and inputs, and disseminates technical information through demonstrations and printed materials. Digital technologies are leveraged to enhance seed marketing and facilitate purchases by smallholder farmers.
Third, AFDP promotes farmer awareness and demand for improved seeds. It aims to reach 200,000 households across 40 districts in 10 regions, focusing on maize, sunflower, and pulses. Through farmer field schools, on-farm demonstrations, seed fairs, and nutrition education, the programme introduces farmers to new technologies and best practices. It also empowers local farmer organizations to provide advisory services and uses digital platforms to disseminate information. Financial services are facilitated to support input purchases.
Finally, the programme strengthens market linkages by fostering partnerships between farmers and agribusinesses. It encourages contract farming and pricing agreements with processors, connects farmers to structured trading platforms like G-Soko, and conducts market mapping studies. Support is also provided to youth entrepreneurs and cooperatives, and technical and business information is widely shared. AFDP collaborates with existing initiatives such as the Agricultural Market Development Trust (AMDT) and the Pan African Bean Research Alliance (PABRA) to maximize impact and promote best practices.

ii) The AFDP programme’s fish market development and value addition component focuses on reducing postharvest losses and increasing income opportunities, particularly for women and youth. It aims to improve infrastructure and introduce technologies that enhance the quality and marketability of fish products. These investments are expected to benefit over 30,000 artisanal fishers, processors, and traders, while creating direct and indirect employment for around 1,000 youth along the tuna value chain.
To achieve this, the programme will co-finance the establishment of eight ice-making plants, three cold chain and processing facilities, ten solar dryers for seaweed and small pelagic fish (dagaa), and 80 dagaa drying racks. Additionally, modern fish markets will be rehabilitated in Pangani and Bagamoyo, modeled after successful markets in Dar es Salaam. These facilities will be managed by cooperatives and small enterprises, with sustainable user-fee systems to ensure proper maintenance and long-term viability.
AFDP will also support access to finance for fishers’ cooperatives and associations through partnerships with financial institutions, facilitated by the Tanzania Agricultural Development Bank (TADB). This will enable investment in equipment, infrastructure, and working capital, with a focus on youth and women-led groups.
In aquaculture, the programme will strengthen farmer clusters and link them with private hatcheries. It will establish aquaculture field schools to train youth and women, promote collective marketing, and improve access to inputs and cold storage. These clusters will coordinate production to ensure a steady supply of fish and engage in local governance and policy advocacy.
For the seaweed sector, which is predominantly female-led, AFDP will address challenges in processing and value addition. It will fund market analyses, strengthen cooperatives, and provide equipment such as drying racks, solar dryers, milling machines, and packaging materials. The programme will also support the development of seaweed-based small enterprises and link them to financial and business services. Partnerships with organizations like The Nature Conservancy and buyers such as Cargill will help scale market access and improve product quality. An inclusive business model from Zanzibar will be adapted to Pemba and mainland Tanzania to promote fair pricing, compliance with standards, and collective bargaining.

projects.name: Support the implementation of sustainable fishing practises, and protection of important fish habitats (Enhanced productivity of fisheries) (part AFDP)
projects.description:
Support sustainable fisheries and aquaculture development in Tanzania mainland and Zanzibar government’s strategic objective of promoting sustainable fish production systems from both capture fisheries and aquaculture. The AFDP Programme’s interventions under this subcomponent supports the livelihoods of 18,000 artisanal fishers, 6,000 fish farmers and 15,000 seaweed producers who are dependent on fisheries and aquaculture. More specifically, the investments will result into (i) increased fish production and productivity; (ii) increased and sustainable income for fisher-folks; (iii) Improved nutrition as a result of increased consumption of fish and fish products; (iv) Increased access the recommended gears suitable for sustainable fishing, ideally to replace destructive gears and aiming to reduce the fishing effort; v) enhanced use of selective fishing practices by the use of Fish Aggregating Devices (FADS); and vi) improved utilization of catch and reduce post-harvest losses.
The programme supports the development of a semi-commercial fishing joint venture through 4Ps’ arrangements between the respective government fishing agencies in Tanzania Mainland (TAFICO) and Zanzibar (ZAFICO), private sector investors and small-scale fishers’ cooperative societies. The Programme will finance the acquisition four  fully equipped long line fishing vessels. An integrated fish processing plant will be designed and equipped with modern technologies to meet the regional and international market standards. AFDP will promotes 4P joint-venture shareholding schemes or supply-based arrangements as a mechanism to include smallholder fishers and fish traders in deep sea fishing and fish processing plants. Between 30-40 percent of the catch is expected to be used in the domestic markets through small scale fishers and other actors involved in 15/31 the fishery value chain including youths and women. On the other hand, small scale fishers will supply bait to the vessels which require sufficient amount of baits during its operations. These investments will generate employment directly and indirectly for about 1 000 youth along the tuna value chain, and will provide services and market outlets to over 15,000 artisanal fishers and their cooperative societies to supply fish and baits. AFDP will intervene through developing the capacity of Aquaculture Development Centers (ADCs) (Kingolwira, Mwamapuli and Rubambagwe) to supply high quality Tilapia and catfish seeds and deliver effective extension services. The programme targets to raise the level of Tilapia fingerlings production to an additional 25 million fingerlings, and 10 million of catfish per year at the end of the six-year investment period. Fresh-water aquaculture interventions under AFDP will focuses on: (i) rehabilitating/developing the basic infrastructure for hatchery production (including water supply systems, access roads, hatchery facilities, feed mill and equipment etc.) in three ADCs (Kingolwira, Mwamapuli and Rubambagwe); (ii) developing the Kinglowira ADC to become a breeding nucleus which will produce quality broodstock to be multiplied in other ADCs and private hatcheries for mass production of fingerlings; (iii) establishing and strengthening aquaculture clusters targeting about 6,000 aquafarmers; and (iv) developing a national aquaculture information system. The Programme adopts a cluster growth model, through which the ADCs will nurture and support growth of private hatcheries and aquaculture service providers. AFDP will invest in (i) carrying out tissue culture and micro-propagation technologies to produce at least one ton annually of cottonii to be multiplied in farmers plots; (ii) promoting of new seaweed production methods supporting about 15 000 women farmers to more deeper waters where E. cottonii farming can successfully be undertaken; and (iii) improving and intensifying the cultivation of E. spinosum to increase current production from 400Kg to up to 1.6 tons per farmer annually, increasing farm size from the current 50 ropes units to on average 400 ropes units per farmer; and (iv) training of over 1,000 youth on mariculture in Zanzibar. The programme will finance the rehabilitation and equipment of ZARI laboratory facilities for tissue culture micro-propagation, field testing and large scale on farm multiplication by trained farmers, small boats and hand pulled plastic barges and /hand pulled for women groups and cooperatives.

children.description:
During the reporting period, in March 2022 the mainland Government reviewed and updated the national social protection policy and implementing strategy. The Government conducted five consultations with  different stakeholders from social assistance; social security; productive inclusion and social insurances.  Currently a cabinet paper has been drafted to be submitted to the cabinet. 
The mid-term review of the  productive social safety net program was successfully carried out in January 2022. PSSN II has expanded coverage from 70 percent to 100 percent to all villages and Shehia in mainland and Zanzibar with an estimated 5,180,684  beneficiaries of which 55.7 percent were females and 44.3 percent were males. The total number of households is 1,375,107.  PSSN II impact evaluation design was completed, and the survey questionnaire developed. A total of 434 villages from 32 PAAs were sampled for the evaluation. Training of enumerators on questionnaire management was done and completed and enumerators deployed to conduct data collection in sampled areas.  Total of 60,779 beneficiaries out of 97,430 were found with high level of disability and confirmed as being eligible for disability benefit and  45,875 disability beneficiaries were paid during the  July/August payment period in 2022.
